title: Fabricating a Kidney Cortex Extracellular Matrix-Derived Hydrogel
protocol: Sterilize a 5000 mL beaker and a 70 x 10 mm stir bar.
Mix sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) at a ratio of 1:1000 (weight:volume) in autoclaved deionized water in the beaker.
Leave the solution on a stir plate at approximately 200 rpm for 24 hours or until SDS is completely dissolved.
Transfer the solution to a 500 mL sterile vacuum filter and filter it into sterilized sealable containers.
Wash and autoclave a pair of forceps, two hemostat clamps, a pair of general service grade scissors, two scalpel blade handles, a 1000 mL beaker covered with aluminum foil, and a 36 x 9 mm stir bar.
Line a tissue culture hood with underpad.
Place the beaker, a sterile tissue culture dish (150 x 25 mm), and the whole kidney organ into the hood.
Fill the beaker with 500 mL of 1% SDS solution.
Place the kidney in the sterile tissue culture dish.
Remove all perirenal fat by lightly shaving around the renal capsule with a scalpel.
Make a shallow 8-10 cm incision with the scalpel to break open the renal capsule without damaging the underlying cortex tissue.
Peel away the renal capsule from the cortex tissue using two hemostat clamps.
Bisect the kidney along the coronal plane using the scalpel along the lateral side of the kidney.
Isolate the cortex tissue from both halves by carving out the medullary region with the scalpel.
Dice the cortex tissue into 0.5 cm³ pieces.
Remove any large visible vessels from the diced cortex tissue.
Fill a 1000 mL beaker with 500 mL of 1% SDS solution.
Place the diced cortex tissue and stir bar into the beaker containing SDS solution.
Cover the beaker with autoclaved aluminum foil.
Stir the beaker at approximately 400 rpm outside of the tissue culture hood for 24 hours.
Bring the beaker into a tissue culture hood after stirring.
Add a 40 µm sterile cell strainer made with nylon mesh to the beaker.
Fill a separate 1000 mL beaker with 200 mL of bleach and place it in the tissue culture hood.
Pipette out the SDS solution through the cell strainer into the beaker containing bleach.
Continue pipetting until only decellularized tissue remains in the beaker.
Leave the cell strainer in the beaker.
Fill the beaker with 500 mL of fresh SDS solution.
Cover the beaker with aluminum foil.
Place the beaker onto a stir plate at the same speed as before.
Repeat steps 1.3.1-1.3.3 every 24 hours with fresh SDS solution for a total of five days.
Rinse decellularized tissue with autoclaved DI water every 24 h for 3 days total, following the technique outlined in steps 1.3.1-1.3.3.
Rinse decellularized tissue with cell culture grade water every 24 h for 2 days total, following the technique outlined in steps 1.3.1-1.3.3.
Repeat steps 1.3.1-1.3.2.
Transfer the decellularized tissue into a 30 mL self-standing conical tube.
Fill the conical tube with cell culture grade water until all the tissue is submerged.
Mechanically homogenize the kECM within the conical tube with a tissue homogenizer for 2 min.
Submerge the conical tube containing the kECM in liquid nitrogen until boiling surrounding the tube no longer persists.
Store the kECM at -4 ˚C overnight.
Slightly loosen the conical tube cap to allow for gas exchange.
Place the conical tube into a lyophilization machine.
Lyophilize the kECM for three days or until it resembles a fine white powder.
Store the lyophilized kECM at -4 ˚C.
Autoclave a 20 mL scintillation vial and cap.
Autoclave a 15.9 x 7.9 mm stir bar.
Autoclave one pair of fine-tip forceps.
Weigh the lyophilized kECM.
Calculate the volume of HCl needed to solubilize the kECM.
Calculate the mass of pepsin required for the solution.
Add porcine gastric pepsin to a scintillation vial in a tissue culture hood.
Add 0.01 N HCl to the scintillation vial.
Add a stir bar to the scintillation vial.
Leave the mixture on a stir plate at approximately 500 rpm until all pepsin has dissolved.
Transfer the lyophilized kECM to the scintillation vial containing pepsin and HCl.
Stir the solution on a stir plate at approximately 500 rpm for three days.
Mix the kECM hydrogel stock solution with 1 N NaOH.
Mix the kECM hydrogel stock solution with 10x Media Supplement (M199).
Mix the kECM hydrogel stock solution with cell culture media.
Keep all solutions on ice during mixing.
Determine the volume of stock kECM hydrogel needed using the equation provided.
Calculate the volume of neutralizing reagents required using the given equations.
Pipette neutralizing reagents (NaOH, M199, and cell culture media) into a sterile 30 mL self-standing conical tube.
Mix the neutralizing reagent solution with a microspatula.
Transfer the appropriate volume of stock kECM hydrogel to the neutralizing reagent solution using a sterile 1 mL syringe.
Gently mix the solution until homogeneous in color using a microspatula.
Avoid introducing air bubbles by stirring slowly and gently.
Suspend cells into 10 µL of cell culture media.
Determine the number of cells to be suspended using the equation provided.
Pipette the 10 µL of cell suspension solution into the final kECM gel after mixing with neutralizing reagent solution.
Stir the solution with a microspatula until cells are evenly distributed.
Fill a desired cell culture device with the kECM hydrogel using a 1 mL syringe.
Allow the gel to set at 37 °C for 1 h before transferring or plating cells.
